subject: capuchin monkey
title: Young Monkeys on an Island Started Kidnapping Babies. Nobody Knows Why

scenes.text: On one island, young monkeys started stealing babies, and they don't eat them.
It's Jicarón, off Panama. Cameras caught a young male capuchin carrying a baby howler monkey on his back.
Researchers named him Joker. He carried one baby for up to nine days.
Then four other young males copied him. In fifteen months, at least eleven babies were taken.
Away from their mothers' milk, at least four of the babies died.
No food, no fight, no reason anyone can find. Scientists think it may simply be a fad.

description:
On Jicarón Island, Panama, camera traps filmed young male white-faced capuchins carrying off at least 11 baby mantled howler monkeys over 15 months. One male, nicknamed Joker, started in 2022 and four others copied him. At least four babies died.
The capuchins don't eat the babies. The study (Current Biology, 2025) suggests the behaviour may be a social fad.
Why do you think they do it?
first_comment: Boredom, practice for parenting, or a fad? What's your theory?
